clue.text: Private eye following tip in Manhattan, perhaps

indicators.note: the detective's word comes after the word for tip, in answer order

parts.note: to cock a hat is to tip or tilt it
a tail is a detective who shadows someone

explanation.surface: A detective trailing a tip-off somewhere in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manhattan' looks like the New York setting of a gumshoe story; here it is the drink, and 'perhaps' flags it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manhattan is a whisky-and-vermouth mixed drink, one example of the category.

clue.text: She's a musical lass at heart

indicators.note: the name sits in the middle of the phrase musical lass, across the word gap

explanation.surface: A girl described as having music at her core.
explanation.walkthrough: The soprano Maria Callas is the 'She'; 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Callas was a famous female opera singer, so she can stand as a cryptic 'She'.

clue.text: Foreign businessman in China beginning to pine for wife in nearby country

indicators.note: one letter standing in for another, the pine letter taking the wife's place

parts.note: Taiwan lies just off the Chinese coast

indicators.note: only the opening letter of pine is used

explanation.surface: A merchant in China pining for a wife back in a neighbouring land.
explanation.definitionFit: A taipan was historically the head of a foreign trading firm operating in China.

clue.text: Evidence in support of Wally is very straightforward

indicators.note: in a down entry, the supporting word sits underneath the other

parts.note: wally is British slang for a fool
evidence that settles a matter is proof

explanation.surface: Testimony backing up a fool is perfectly plain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'in support of' puts PROOF below IDIOT. A 'wally' is everyday British slang for a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so simple that nobody could get it wrong is described with this compound adjective.

clue.text: Eugene's gone mad at home

definitions.note: the definition names Eugene's surname, the possessive pointing to what belongs to him

indicators.note: going mad suggests the letters of gone are scrambled

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone called Eugene has lost his mind indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene Onegin is Pushkin's verse-novel hero (and Tchaikovsky's opera); the surname is 'Eugene's'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Pushkin's work is Eugene, and this is his family name.

clue.text: He plays bridge with Eric's little mate from Lancashire, perhaps

parts.note: the four bridge players are named North, South, East and West
Eric Morecambe called his comedy partner Ernie Wise 'little Ern'

explanation.surface: A card player teams up with a comic's sidekick from the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe and Wise were a famous British comedy double act; Eric often called Ernie 'little Ern'. Lancashire is an English county in the north-west.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire lies in northern England, so its people are one example of the adjective.

clue.text: Produce model teenager

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters of teenager are reshaped

explanation.surface: A young fashion model put forward as the product.
explanation.definitionFit: To produce something and to bring it into being are synonyms.

clue.text: Nuts and nori ultimately very suitable for vegans

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of and nori go wild
the final letter of very is taken

explanation.surface: Nuts and seaweed make good food for people who avoid animal products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like a food on the vegan menu, but it is the anagram signal on AND NORI.
explanation.definitionFit: Food with no milk products is suitable for those avoiding animal produce, though vegans also avoid meat and eggs.

clue.text: Poet's written about return of Irish hooligan

indicators.note: the poet's name is written around another piece

parts.note: Philip Larkin was an English poet; 's stands for has

indicators.note: the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A poet has written about an Irish ruffian coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' reverses the Irish abbreviation before Larkin's name is written around it; 'hooligan' is the Australian sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Larrikin is Australian slang for a rowdy, mischievous young man, a hooligan.

clue.text: He wrote novels about samurai

parts.note: c (circa) means about
a ronin is a samurai without a master

explanation.surface: An author whose novels concern Japanese warriors.
explanation.walkthrough: A J Cronin was a Scottish novelist (The Citadel).
explanation.definitionFit: A J Cronin was a twentieth-century Scottish author of popular novels.

clue.text: Olympic venue playing host to a legendary runner

indicators.note: the city takes the letter in, as a host takes in a guest

parts.note: Atlanta hosted the 1996 Olympic Games

explanation.surface: An Olympic city welcomes a famous athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, Atalanta was a swift huntress beaten in a footrace only by a trick with golden apples.

clue.text: Ordered hair to be hidden in Saudi Arabia: it's the law

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are tucked inside the country abbreviation
ordered means put in order, rearranging the letters of hair

explanation.surface: Women in Saudi Arabia are ordered to cover their hair by law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like a command about covering hair, but it is the anagram signal; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharia is Islamic religious law, the legal code in force in Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: Col acted in remake of Western

indicators.note: a remake reworks the material, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A colonel took a role in a new version of a cowboy film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' looks like the film genre; here it is the adjective meaning of the West.
explanation.definitionFit: Occidental means belonging to the West, the opposite of oriental.

clue.text: Legal official and professional custodian

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a curator is the keeper of a collection

explanation.surface: A lawyer who is also a paid keeper of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A procurator is an agent or officer of the law, such as a Scottish public prosecutor.

clue.text: Gay hero's informal address for former PM

parts.note: Mac is a casual way to address a man
Edward Heath was UK prime minister 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: A gay man's casual nickname for an ex-prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gay' is John Gay, author of The Beggar's Opera, whose hero is the highwayman Macheath; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Macheath is the leading man of John Gay's ballad opera, so he is Gay's hero.

clue.text: Scotsman is embraced by a star

indicators.note: the outer star name wraps around the short word

parts.note: Altair is a bright star in Aquila

explanation.surface: A Scottish man is hugged by a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a star' looks like a celebrity; it is Altair, one particular star.
explanation.definitionFit: Alistair is the Scottish form of Alexander, a typically Scottish man's name.

clue.text: A protein, possibly a poison

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of a protein may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Suspecting that a protein might be toxic.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a toxic alkaloid from deadly nightshade.

clue.text: Taking more than one form and consisting of a pair of lines, circle and imaginary line

parts.note: L is line, so two lines are LL
O is circle-shaped
the tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are imaginary lines of latitude

explanation.surface: Describing something shape-shifting built of lines and a circle, like a geometry diagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotropic element exists in several physical forms, as carbon does as diamond and graphite.

clue.text: Regret mental breakdown

indicators.note: a breakdown breaks the letters of mental apart for reassembly

explanation.surface: Feeling sorry after a nervous breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament is to mourn or express sorrow, a synonym of regret.

clue.text: Order Lambert to be detained in fortress

indicators.note: the unit symbol is held inside the class word

parts.note: a caste is a social order or class
L is the symbol for the lambert, a unit of luminance

explanation.surface: A man called Lambert is ordered locked up in a fort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command; it is CASTE, a social order, which holds L.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle is a fortified building, a fortress.

clue.text: Write note about ensign

parts.note: to pen is to write
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Composing a short message about a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow flag or banner, as is an ensign.

clue.text: Cathy's so passionate about plant

indicators.note: the answer is found about, i.e. in among, the words Cathy's so passionate

explanation.surface: Cathy is so keen on a certain plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant runs across catHY'S SO Passionate.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyssop is an aromatic herb of the mint family.

clue.text: Individual has a part to play in office

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for office

parts.note: a see is a bishop's office or seat

indicators.note: letting the letters play rearranges a part

explanation.surface: Someone with a role to fill in an office job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'office' is a bishop's see, not a workplace; 'to play' is the anagram signal and 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate and individual both mean distinct and apart from others.

clue.text: Arabian novelist's fictional soldier

parts.note: Kingsley and Martin Amis are English novelists

explanation.surface: An Arab writer's made-up soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Aramis is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramis is one of the musketeers in Dumas's novel, a soldier in fiction.

clue.text: Former England captain makes another broadcast about one of team

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the single letter
broadcast means scattered, so the letters of another are spread around
a single letter of team, its first, is taken

explanation.surface: An ex-skipper makes another radio programme about a team member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges ANOTHER into ATHERON, which goes about T from 'one of team'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike Atherton captained the England cricket team in the 1990s.

clue.text: "Doctor Thorne" has a sting in the tail

definitions.text: has a sting in the tail
definitions.note: a descriptive definition: a creature that has a sting at its rear

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, rearranging the letters of Thorne

explanation.surface: Trollope's novel Doctor Thorne has a surprise ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Thorne' looks like the Trollope title, but 'Doctor' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hornet is a large wasp whose stinger is at the rear of its abdomen.

clue.text: A couple of slackers natter about untidy girl

indicators.note: the first two letters of slackers are taken
the letters of natter are turned about

explanation.surface: Two idlers chat about a messy young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A slattern is a dated term for a slovenly, untidy woman.
